elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 as rendered still binds Ono and its Affiliates: "neither Ono or its Affiliates ... shall Commercialize in the Ono Territory: (i) a product that includes ... an agent that is a [ * ] ...", and the new sentence expressly preserves "Ono's obligations ... under this Section 8.2". A restriction on Customer remains, so the preferred (no restriction) position is not reached.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence only redefines the label ("For purposes of Ono's obligations and Array's remedies under this Section 8.2, Competing Product means only a product, other than a Product, that includes Binimetinib or Encorafenib as an active pharmaceutical ingredient"), while the retained operative prohibition in the opening sentence continues to bar Ono from Commercializing the class-based products described in clauses (i) and (ii) ("an agent that is a [ * ]"). Worse, that retained language expressly carves the named compounds OUT of the class ("other than Binimetinib", "other than Encorafenib"), so the new definition contradicts, rather than narrows, the retained prohibition. The restriction on Ono is therefore still class-based (and internally inconsistent), not limited to a named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: "Ono's and its Affiliates' obligations under this Section 8.2 shall apply only during the term of this Agreement", and the former post-termination extension ("prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect") has been deleted.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "shall in no event extend beyond the twelve (12) month anniversary of the Effective Date" – an outer cap of twelve months, and no post-term tail survives.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: "shall not restrict (i) Ono's or its Affiliates' internal research or Development activities".
"shall not restrict ... (ii) any product or program acquired by Ono or its Affiliates through any acquisition of or merger with a Third Party".

reasons: Scope prong fails: the edit narrows only the defined term "Competing Product" for Ono's obligations, but the actual prohibition in the first sentence of Section 8.2 operates on its own class description ("an agent that is a [ * ]") and is left untouched, so Ono remains subject to a class-wide, redaction-defined field-of-use restriction.

Internal contradiction: the retained opening sentence excludes Binimetinib- and Encorafenib-containing products from the restricted class ("other than Binimetinib" / "other than Encorafenib"), while the inserted definition says the restriction covers only products containing Binimetinib or Encorafenib. The two sentences cannot both be given effect, leaving the scope of Ono's covenant indeterminate.

Repair in operative language: amend the opening sentence itself so that, as applied to Ono and its Affiliates, the prohibition reads on a product (other than a Product) containing Binimetinib or Encorafenib as an active pharmaceutical ingredient (or otherwise expressly disapply clauses (i) and (ii) to Ono), rather than redefining the label downstream; and delete or reconcile the "(other than Binimetinib)"/"(other than Encorafenib)" carve-outs so they do not contradict the narrowed Ono covenant.

Also confirm the temporal anchor for Ono: the opening lead-in "Prior to the [ * ]" remains a redacted, undefined trigger; the new sentence overrides it for Ono, but the drafter should state expressly that the redacted period does not apply to Ono to avoid a competing anchor.

Term and 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs are all present and satisfactory; only the named-product scope prong (and the resulting inconsistency) blocks fallback completion.

Minimality is satisfied: the change deletes only the post-termination extension and adds two sentences directed at the checklist elements; Array's reciprocal class-wide restriction, the royalty-termination consequence and Array's Section 8.2 termination right are retained.
